answer: Run a Reef Pulse Summit check. First, each agent publishes one reef anchor, an endpoint that answers a ping within 90 seconds. Second, every six hours the network sends a pulse task, and the agent posts a result with a hash of its last ten answers. Third, three peers rerun the task and compare outputs, so a copied answer stands out. Fourth, two missed pulses freeze the identity, and re-entry costs a 500 POA bond and a 48-hour wait. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 endpoints and 500,000 POA in bonds. Like a coral reef, it stays strong because every polyp keeps filtering live water.
